subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Fetal Growth Restriction and Umbilical Artery Doppler

steps.tx: Failure of a fetus to reach its growth potential from placental insufficiency is **fetal growth restriction**. It differs from constitutional smallness, though both appear as small measurements. Stillbirth and neonatal complications concentrate in the truly restricted group. Customised charts adjust for maternal height, weight and parity and catch more truly restricted babies than population charts.
steps.say: Fetal growth restriction fails growth potential from placental insufficiency, unlike constitutional smallness.

steps.tx: Early even slowing of head and body from chronic undernutrition before twenty eight weeks gives **symmetric IUGR** in older terminology. Causes include chromosomal, infectious and severe early placental disease. Modern practice describes timing and Doppler pattern instead. Chromosomal causes include triploidy and trisomy 18, where growth failure shows at the anomaly scan.
steps.say: Symmetric IUGR slows head and body evenly from early chronic causes.

steps.tx: Head sparing late growth failure from placental insufficiency is **asymmetric IUGR**. Blood is redistributed to brain at the expense of liver and fat stores. Abdominal circumference falls first while head growth persists. The cerebroplacental ratio captures this sparing numerically, brain flow rising as abdominal growth falls.
steps.say: Asymmetric IUGR spares the head while abdominal growth falls from placental failure.

steps.tx: The waveform in this picture is a placenta failing in slow motion. **Absent end diastolic flow** in the umbilical artery means resistance downstream has risen until forward flow stops between heartbeats, and reversal is graver still. Each stage shortens the safe interval before delivery, whatever the fetal size. Serial Doppler therefore times preterm delivery in growth restriction more honestly than any single estimate of weight can.
steps.say: Absent or reversed end diastolic flow marks rising placental resistance in growth restriction. Serial Doppler times delivery more honestly than weight alone.

vis.alt: Umbilical artery Doppler waveform in fetal growth restriction showing absent end diastolic flow.
vis.caption: An umbilical Doppler trace shows flow vanishing between heartbeats in severe placental insufficiency. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Placental resistance reflected in the umbilical waveform is measured by **umbilical artery Doppler**. Rising resistance reduces diastolic flow progressively. It is the primary surveillance tool in growth restriction. An umbilical pulsatility index above the 95th centile for gestation is the abnormal threshold used in reports.
steps.say: Umbilical artery Doppler reflects placental resistance as the primary surveillance tool.

vis.alt: Umbilical artery Doppler progression in growth restriction, from reduced to reversed end-diastolic flow.
vis.caption: Umbilical artery Doppler progression in growth restriction, from reduced to reversed end-diastolic flow. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Complete disappearance of forward flow in diastole is **absent end-diastolic flow**. It signals advanced placental disease and high stillbirth risk within days to weeks. Delivery timing balances this against prematurity by gestation. With absent flow at 32 weeks, delivery usually follows steroids rather than waiting for reversal to appear.
steps.say: Absent end-diastolic flow signals advanced placental disease needing delivery timing decisions.

steps.tx: Flow actually reversing in diastole, the gravest umbilical pattern, is **reversed flow**. At early gestations it may prompt immediate delivery discussions at viability limits. Ductus venosus changes refine timing further. Reversed flow before 30 weeks occurs in only a small minority, and ductus venosus then decides timing day by day.
steps.say: Reversed flow is the gravest umbilical pattern and may prompt delivery at viability limits.

steps.tx: Brain sparing redistribution lowering middle cerebral resistance is the **cerebroplacental ratio** concept. A low ratio signals fetal adaptation to hypoxia. It adds prediction in late growth restriction where umbilical flow may stay normal. A ratio under 1.0, or below the fifth centile, is the usual abnormal cut off quoted.
steps.say: The cerebroplacental ratio detects brain sparing in late growth restriction.

steps.tx: Serial growth scans every two to three weeks track velocity because single measurements mislead, following **interval growth assessment**. Crossing centiles downward confirms restriction better than one small reading. Fluid volume trends accompany the biometry. Scans closer than two weeks apart mostly measure error, because true growth needs time to declare itself.
steps.say: Interval growth assessment tracks velocity because single small measurements mislead.

steps.tx: Delivery is the only treatment, timed to maximise maturity before stillbirth, the principle of **timed delivery**. Steroids and magnesium precede early deliveries. Growth restriction at term needs delivery by thirty seven to thirty eight weeks even with normal Doppler. Late restriction at term with normal umbilical Doppler still carries stillbirth risk, which is why induction is offered.
steps.say: Timed delivery balances maturity against stillbirth, with term restriction delivered by thirty eight weeks.
